title: Runtime contracts and ABI stability - arch review
content:
Meeting purpose: go through the proposed runtime API/ABI contract for the serving runtime and model bundles, align on compatibility guarantees, and decide rollout and enforcement strategy for v1.0 of the contract.

Date: 2025-02-12
Attendees: Aisha Menon (chair), Carlos Rivera, Jun Park, Lena Hoffman, Priya Shah, Samir Gupta (remote), Diego Alvarez (notes)

Agenda:
- Quick recap of proposed contract surface (what’s in scope for v1)
- Backwards/forwards compatibility guarantees and allowed breaking changes
- Schema negotiation / version negotiation flow for model bundles
- Enforcement: validation gates, CI checks, runtime fallbacks
- Rollout plan and canary strategy across Dedicated and Private deployments
- Open questions and next actions

Recap of proposed surface (Jun presented):
- Two layers of contract:
  - Model bundle manifest schema (metadata, required entrypoints, expected KV formats)
  - Runtime ABI (the on-disk and in-memory conventions for tensors, kv cache keys, and plugin hooks)
- Manifest v1 fields are intentionally minimal: model-id, model-version, entrypoint (e.g., "generate", "chat"), encoder-type, tokenizer-spec-ref, optional quantization-hint, declared-dependencies (list of required kernels/extensions)
- ABI guarantees: same tensor layout (row-major float32 baseline), plugin entrypoints must register via the runtime plugin registry with semver-style interface IDs

Key decisions agreed (high-level):
1) Semver-based contract versioning and a compatibility matrix will be published. We will treat the manifest (bundle metadata) and runtime ABI separately for versioning.
2) Backwards compatibility guarantee: runtime vX must support model bundles declared as bundle-manifest <= X (manifest version). For ABI, we commit to stable tensor layout and plugin call signatures within a major release; minor releases can add optional fields but must not remove required fields.
3) For forward compatibility (older runtime loading newer bundle): allow negotiated fallbacks where possible, but treat new-required fields as fatal unless a compatibility shim is present. Shims will be implemented as part of platform-engineering for a small set of common changes (e.g., tokenizer-ref semantics).
4) Validation gates: every model bundle artifact must pass a preflight validator in CI that checks manifest schema, dependency declarations, and a smoke-run via lightweight container using the runtime-mock harness. Bundles that fail schema validation will be rejected from the artifact registry.

Discussion highlights and rationale:
- Carlos argued that making the manifest minimal reduces churn for model teams and allows the runtime to evolve without breaking everything. This was accepted but with a caveat: optional fields must have precise semantics documented (behavioral notes).
- Priya raised concerns about quantization hints. We decided quantization-hint remains advisory; enforcement lives in the serving runtime's scheduling policy (i.e., we may route quantized bundles only to certain worker pools).
- Jun proposed a plugin ABI where plugins declare a 4-tuple: (name, interface-version, exported-hooks, capability-bitmask). The group pushed back on capability-bitmask complexity; we will start with explicit hooks list and move to capability flags in v2 after usage telemetry.

Schema negotiation flow (agreed):
- On bundle load, runtime reads manifest.version and compares against supported_manifest_versions.
  - If manifest.version <= max_supported_minor_of_runtime_major then load normally.
  - If manifest.version > supported -> if a declared compatibility-shim exists for (runtime.major, manifest.version) attempt shim; otherwise reject.
- For plugin/version mismatches, runtime will attempt dynamic compatibility mapping for minor version differences (<1.0.0 semantics). Major version mismatches require explicit opt-in or shim.

Enforcement and CI strategy:
- Add pre-commit and CI checks in the model packaging pipeline (PR checks) that run: schema-lint, dependency-validator, smoke-run on runtime-mock (containerized), and integration test for plugin API surface used by the bundle.
- Add an artifact registry webhook that performs runtime-version compatibility checks before promoting to internal release channels.
- The runtime binary will expose a diagnostic endpoint (/compat-check) that can simulate loading a bundle manifest and report detailed compatibility issues; teams can call this during packaging.

Rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 (now -> 2 weeks): finalize manifest schema and publish doc. Implement schema-lint in packaging repo.
Phase 1 (2-6 weeks): add CI smoke-run harness and artifact registry webhook. Start gating internal model rollouts in dev clusters.
Phase 2 (6-10 weeks): enable runtime /compat-check endpoint in staging; test shims for tokenizer-ref and quantization-hint.
Phase 3 (10-18 weeks): enable enforced rejection for invalid bundles in Dedicated test clusters and deploy canary to 5% of hosted traffic.
Phase 4 (18+ weeks): full enforcement across hosted, optional enforcement in Dedicated with an opt-in period for customers. Private (on-prem) customers get a compat-check tool but enforcement depends on their upgrade policy.

Canary strategy specifics:
- Canary bundles first in internal dev cluster for 48h smoke tests (perf and correctness).
- Promote to Dedicated test ring (10% of Dedicated capacity) for 7 days with close telemetry on Tensor layout mismatches, memory regression, and plugin exception rates.
- For hosted, use routing policies to route a small percentage (initial 0.5%) of real traffic and shadow requests from 10% of traffic to the new code path for metric comparison.

Open technical risks and mitigations:
- Risk: subtle change in tensor layout conventions could cause silent corruption. Mitigation: include a binary-level checksum test for tensors in smoke-run harness, add an opt-in strict-layout flag that disables automatic layout conversions.
- Risk: plugin authoring errors can crash worker processes. Mitigation: run plugins in isolated sandboxes (already planned), add stronger runtime plugin interface validation and fuzz tests.
- Risk: customers on old private deployments may not upgrade, causing support burden. Mitigation: provide compat-check CLI and detailed migration guides; offer professional services for complex shim development.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Finalize manifest v1 schema doc (Aisha) due 2025-02-18
- Add schema-lint rule to model-packaging repo (Carlos) due 2025-02-20
- Implement runtime-mock smoke-run container and CI job (Jun) due 2025-02-28
- Implement artifact-registry webhook prototype (Lena) due 2025-03-05
- Add /compat-check diagnostic endpoint to runtime (Samir) due 2025-03-12
- Draft migration guidance for quantization-hint and tokenizer-ref (Priya) due 2025-03-01

Notes for follow-up meeting:
- Review metrics from runtime-mock smoke runs (Jun) and update shim list based on top breakages.
- Decide on telemetry fields to include in compatibility reports (suggested: layout-checksum, required-kernel-list, plugin-versions).
- Plan customer-facing communications for Dedicated and Private enforcement timelines.

Meeting adjourned at 11:40am. Next check-in scheduled 2025-02-26 10:00am (arch sync).

Internal references and quick links:
- Runtime compatibility RFC draft: CONFLUENCE-PLAT/runtime-contracts-v1
- Packaging pipeline repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-packaging
- Related Linear ticket: PLAT-391

Appendix: quick glossary
- bundle manifest: JSON/YAML artifact that describes model artifact and runtime hints
- shim: code path in runtime or packaging that adapts newer bundle fields to older runtime expectations
- strict-layout flag: runtime option to fail on tensor layout mismatches instead of attempting auto-conversion
